_comment: USB flash controller VID:PID database. Note: a VID:PID identifies the USB bridge mode the controller is currently in, not the controller SKU itself. The same SoC can expose many VID:PIDs depending on how it was mass-produced. Use ChipGenius or physical chip markings for authoritative ID. PRs welcome.

vendors.346d: Unknown / no-name OEM — common on cheap Chinese sticks

058f:6387.notes: Common bridge VID:PID for Alcor controllers in boot mode. Often appears when firmware is corrupt.

058f:9380.notes: USB 3.0 Alcor controller common in no-name retail sticks.

090c:1000.notes: Fallback VID:PID when SMI firmware is corrupt or in mass-production mode. Plug in and SMI MPTool should auto-detect.

090c:3350.notes: USB 3.2 Gen2 SMI; found in newer high-end retail drives.

0781:5591.family: SanDisk Cruzer Blade / Fit (Phison or in-house ASIC depending on year)
0781:5591.tool: Phison MPALL if Phison; SanDisk does not publish their own tool
0781:5591.notes: SanDisk retail bridge; actual controller varies — open the drive to confirm.

0781:5583.tool: Depends on controller — open and read markings

0951:1666.family: Kingston DataTraveler G3 — typically Phison PS2251-13 or PS2251-50
0951:1666.tool: Phison MPALL (match IC version from GetInfo)
0951:1666.notes: Very common controller in Kingston DT series. Open to confirm exact PS2251 revision.

13fe:4300.notes: Common on cheap OEM Kingston-branded sticks sold in packs.

13fe:5500.tool: Phison MPALL / UPTool (match IC version from GetInfo output)
13fe:5500.notes: USB 3.x Phison controller in mass-production / boot ROM mode. Already in a flashable state — MPALL will see it without TP pin shorting. Confirmed in-field 2026-11-01 via ioreg (USB Product Name='2309 Boot ROM', USB Vendor Name='Phison'). Common on Kingston DataTraveler Exodia and various rebrands.

1908:0320.family: Phison PS2251-50 or related USB 3.0 SKU

1e4e:0801.tool: UMPTool or Realtek USB MP Tool

0bda:0180.family: Realtek RTS5171 (card reader; sometimes seen on flash sticks)

14cd:1212.family: SMI SM32xx on Super Top-labeled drives

346d:5678.family: Unknown no-name OEM — physical inspection required
346d:5678.tool: ChipGenius on Windows first (to identify), then matching MPTool
346d:5678.notes: Generic 'USB / Disk 20' USB descriptor is a lazy-OEM fingerprint, extremely common on cheap Chinese sticks. bcdUSB=2.1 compliant but Device Speed=HighSpeed only, i.e. USB 2.0 hardware. Open the drive to read chip markings (see docs/01) BEFORE any firmware operation; the controller family cannot be inferred from the USB descriptor alone. Observed in-field 2026-11-01 as two separate drives sharing this VID:PID (serials FC1659EC33C17 and FC0154F669999).
